summary: @servicetitan/schema-comparison preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `scripts.preinstall` invokes `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime binary from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...` to a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` (~727KB) shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated with a rotated string array (`n7gIxM`), a custom decoder function (`hc1jfK9`) using a scrambled character alphabet, and a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header indicating it is a Bun-only bundle unreadable by standard Node tooling. `setup.mjs` itself is separately obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and inline lookup objects hiding basic operations. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: install-time execution of an opaque payload under a freshly-downloaded interpreter bypasses Node-based review. The package sits under the `@servicetitan/` scope with `publishConfig.access: restricted` and an empty description, consistent with a dependency-confusion squat targeting ServiceTitan's internal registry — installers that resolve this scope from the public registry auto-execute the payload on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
